stage: Follow-up after reviewing the six registered first-round results. This is a secondary comparison on the same common500.
question: Can the receiver infer a variable source scale from the normalized data instead of supplying a population constant? Does an explicit image-scale observation still help?
training: Same fixed 256 validation sources and validation seed 281099 at both 4 and 10 dB. One closed-form ridge per arm with mean-squared validation objective, regularization .1 (features standardized), no search. Frozen transmission and neural receivers.
features: 96 per-channel received normalized latent means and 96 RMS, mean and standard deviation of estimated channel magnitude, estimated receiver SNR, and one scalar column. Last column is always zero for fixed-phase arm; for varying-phase arm it is the native phase-derived scale. No original image or true power available to test estimator.
evaluation: Retain common500, seeds 281101/281102, matching complete frontend source pixels, fading, noise and frozen model. Reuse native and constant controls from first round. Compare native vs inferred-only, signaled+inferred vs inferred-only, and each against its own control, 5000 direct image bootstrap as first round. Fixed clipping [.4,7]. All source, quality and power checks retained.
budget: One A800, 4 physical CPU cores, at most 1800 elapsed GPU seconds. Record actual exit. No neural weight updates.
